To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electronic behavior and localization of stretched DNA are strongly affected by the presence of the external forces, and that the electronic properties of the stretched DNA can be described in terms of a simple tight-binding model with disorder.

1) the electronic structure of the bases and base pairs is significantly affected by stretching of the DNA double helical structure, and that 2) the resulting disorder in the tight-binding model for electron hopping leads to localization of electrons, which is more effective for stretched DNA than for the unstretched structure.

the DNA helical structure, when stretched, leads to a significant decrease in the localization length, which can be as small as 0.1 nm in the stretched form, compared with a few nm in the unstretched form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of external forces on the electronic properties of the double helix.
the electronic behavior of DNA in the stretched state.
the development of a multiscale approach to study electron transport in DNA, and in particular in stretched DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stretched DNA is more susceptible to electron localization and, therefore, to charge transport interruption, than its unstretched counterpart.
the DNA double helical structure is a very effective electron conductor in the absence of external forces.
the electronic behavior and localization of stretched DNA can be understood in terms of the effects of external forces on the electronic states of the DNA bases and base-pairs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electronic behavior of stretched DNA is very sensitive to the relative positions of the bases and to environmental effects.
electronic states in DNA are strongly affected by the presence of water molecules on the DNA backbone and by the structural features of the DNA substrate.
electronic states of DNA bases, and the electronic properties of DNA molecules, are sensitive to structural distortions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, even though the electronic properties of DNA are strongly influenced by the environment, it is possible to capture the main features of the electronic behavior by a simple model that can be used for a variety of applications.
, in the presence of external forces, DNA can be considered a highly disordered material.
the electronic behavior of stretched DNA is qualitatively different from the equilibrium DNA.
